description: Official Python SDK and CLI for the Lenz Verification API (/extract, /assess, /verify, /citecheck, /review, /ask) — verify factual claims and citations in AI- and human-written documents against independent sources.
rules: Install with `pip install lenz-io` (or `pipx install "lenz-io[cli]"` for the CLI) and import `from lenz_io import Lenz, AsyncLenz`.
The client reads `LENZ_API_KEY` (`lenz_...`) from the environment by default (`Lenz()`).

Use `client.assess(claim=...)` or `client.assess(claims=[...])` for fast (~15s) multi-model triage returning `claims` with `verdict`, `confidence`, `rationale`, `searched_pages`, and `suggested_rewrite`.

Use `client.verify_and_wait(claim=...)` for deep sourced verification (takes about a minute or two, returning `verdict`, `lenz_score` 1-10 or `None` on 'No Public Record', `confidence`, `key_finding`, `executive_summary`, and `sources`).

Use `client.review_and_wait(text=..., max_citations=20)` (text or URL) or `client.review_file_and_wait("report.docx")` to verify claims and citations across a document (`review.outcome`, `review.issues`, `review.citation_issues`).

Use `client.citecheck_and_wait(draft, max_citations=10)` or `client.citecheck_and_wait(pairs=[{"statement": ..., "url": ...}])` to verify URLs, DOIs, and legal citations (`cite`) against their sources.
When `verdict == "No Public Record"`, `lenz_score` is `None` — no public record in the evidence settles the claim, which does not make it false.
